title: Banach-space interlude: Fredholm operators and Smale's Sard theorem
summary: Normed and Banach spaces, bounded operators, the Hahn–Banach, open mapping and closed graph theorems as tools; compact operators and Arzelà–Ascoli; Fredholm operators and the index; Banach manifolds; Smale's Sard theorem for Fredholm maps.

objectives.description: Use Banach-space completeness, bounded inverse and compactness with their correct hypotheses.
Compute a Fredholm index, prove its local stability by block elimination, and explain compact parametrices.
Derive the local finite-dimensional reduction of a smooth Fredholm map and state Sard–Smale with the Fredholm and countability hypotheses.

preparation.description: Read lecture 15: §16.1 basic definitions (normed and Banach spaces, bounded operators, Hahn–Banach, open mapping, closed graph) and §16.2 compact operators with Arzelà–Ascoli.
Read lectures 16–17: §16.3 Fredholm operators, Definition 16.13 and the characterisation Theorem 16.26.
Read lectures 18–19: §17 Smale's Sard theorem, Definitions 17.1–17.2, Theorem 17.3.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Every smooth map of Banach manifolds has a residual set of regular values.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Sard–Smale requires a Fredholm map and countability hypotheses. The finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel are essential to its reduction.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Compact operators are Fredholm because they resemble finite-dimensional matrices.
commonMisconceptions.correction: An infinite-dimensional compact diagonal operator can have dense nonclosed range and fail Fredholmness. Identity plus compact, rather than compact alone, is the standard Fredholm example.
